results.q: What happens when a TCP segment has a bad checksum?
answer: Invalid data is caught in tcp_input() (src/core/tcp_in.c:164): it checks `chksum != 0`, and when that is true it records it (`TCP_STATS_INC(tcp.chkerr)`) and jumps to `dropped` (line 588), where it calls pbuf_free() and records it (`TCP_STATS_INC(tcp.drop)`, `MIB2_STATS_INC(mib2.tcpinerrs)`), skipping the rest of tcp_input().
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: lwip_htons(), pbuf_remove_header(), ackno, flags, recv_acked — the previous values stay in place.

Bad input is also rejected in other places: ip4_input() drops it when `inet_chksum(iphdr, iphdr_hlen) != 0` (src/core/ipv4/ip4.c:534), counting it in stats_proto.drop, stats_mib2.ipinhdrerrors; icmp_input() drops it when `inet_chksum_pbuf(p) != 0` (src/core/ipv4/icmp.c:147), counting it in stats_mib2.icmpinerrors, stats_proto.chkerr.

results.q: How is the IPv4 header checksum verified?
answer: It is verified in ip4_input() (src/core/ipv4/ip4.c:534): it checks `inet_chksum(iphdr, iphdr_hlen) != 0`, using inet_chksum(); when that check fails it records it (`IP_STATS_INC(ip.drop)`, `MIB2_STATS_INC(mib2.ipinhdrerrors)`, `IP_STATS_INC(ip.chkerr)`) and calls pbuf_free() and returns.

inet_chksum() (src/core/inet_chksum.c:554) — inet_chksum: Calculates the Internet checksum over a portion of memory. Used primarily for IP and ICMP. @param dataptr start of the buffer to calculate the checksum (no alignment needed) @param len length of the buffer to calculate the checksum @return checksum (as u16_t) to be saved directly in the protocol header.
Step by step, it calls lwip_standard_chksum() (line 557); then it returns `(u16_t)~(unsigned int)LWIP_CHKSUM(dataptr, len)` (line 557).
